entries.name: Volatility-targeted Bitcoin
entries.registered: rule and pass bar written down and pushed before the run (2026-11-11 01:20 UTC)
entries.idea: Hold Bitcoin, but hold less of it when it has recently been jumping around, aiming for a smoother ride.
entries.period: Last 30% of Bitcoin's history (never used to design the rule)

results.k: Sharpe (return per unit of risk), rule vs holding

conditions.rule: Sharpe at least 0.10 above holding
Worst drop at least 10 points shallower
Return at least 70% of holding's
Beats simply holding less Bitcoin

entries.reading: Reacting to volatility added nothing over just holding a bit less Bitcoin.
entries.not_verified: Cash earned nothing in the test. Fees were modelled; real trading would differ.

entries.name: Crypto momentum (top 5 of 28 coins)
entries.idea: Each week, hold the five coins that rose most over the last 90 days.
entries.period: Last 30% of the history of 28 coins

conditions.rule: Sharpe at least 0.15 above holding every coin
Sharpe above holding Bitcoin
Return at least Bitcoin's
Beats 95% of random 5-coin picks

entries.reading: It beat random picking and the whole list, but took more risk than Bitcoin for it.
entries.not_verified: The coin list is coins that exist today, so dead coins are missing and the result is flattered by an unknown amount.

entries.name: Momentum with a Bitcoin trend filter
entries.idea: The same momentum rule, but only invested while Bitcoin is above its 200-day average; otherwise cash.
entries.period: Last 30% of the history of 28 coins

conditions.rule: Sharpe at least 0.15 above the gated list
Sharpe above holding Bitcoin
Worst drop shallower than Bitcoin's
Beats 95% of gated random picks
Return above zero, at least 30 trades

entries.reading: A near miss: better on most counts, but the worst drop was still deeper than Bitcoin's, which was the reason for the filter. Closed, not retuned.
entries.not_verified: Same survivorship flattery as above. This was the second look at one idea, so a pass would have counted for less.

entries.name: Bitcoin funding carry (market-neutral)
entries.registered: commit 539ca0e, simulator committed before the run (4833b9f)
entries.idea: Hold Bitcoin and short the matching futures contract to collect its funding payments, switching on only when payments beat Treasury bills.

results.k: Always holding the carry, per year

conditions.rule: Beats bills by at least 1 point a year
Worst drop no deeper than 3%
At least as good as always holding the carry

entries.reading: Funding paid well in 2024 but less than bills this past year, and the 11 switches cost more in fees than they earned.
entries.not_verified: Exchange, price-mismatch and liquidation risk are not modelled. One market cycle of data.

entries.name: Bitcoin only while US net liquidity is rising
entries.registered: commit 76c2805; runner and tests committed before the run (f5fafec)
entries.idea: Hold Bitcoin only in weeks when the Federal Reserve's balance sheet, less the Treasury's cash account and the overnight reverse repo, is higher than 13 weeks earlier; otherwise sit in cash.
entries.period: Last 30% of Bitcoin's history (2023-06-22 to 2026-11-13, never used to design the rule)

results.k: Random timing with the same exposure that did as well or better

conditions.rule: Sharpe at least 0.10 above holding
Beats 95% of randomly shifted copies of its own timing
Worst drop at least 10 points shallower than holding
Return above zero and at least 10 switches

entries.reading: Whether liquidity was rising did not time Bitcoin. The rule sat in cash 57% of the time, earned about a fifth of what holding earned, avoided none of the worst drop, and random timing with the same exposure did as well or better 62% of the time.
entries.not_verified: One of several popular ways to define net liquidity, one lookback, today's version of the Fed's data, and about three years of Bitcoin with only a few liquidity swings. Cash earned nothing in the test.

entries.name: Bitcoin only while miners are not capitulating
entries.registered: commit 9567b02; runner and tests committed before the run (7b2d904)
entries.idea: Hold Bitcoin only on days when the 30-day average of the network's mining power (hash rate) is at or above its 60-day average; otherwise sit in cash.
entries.period: Last 30% of Bitcoin's history (2023-06-22 to 2026-11-13, never used to design the rule)

results.k: Random timing with the same exposure that did as well or better

conditions.rule: Sharpe at least 0.10 above holding
Beats 95% of randomly shifted copies of its own timing
Worst drop at least 10 points shallower than holding
Return above zero and at least 6 switches

entries.reading: Mining power did not time Bitcoin. In these years it hovered and jittered, so the rule flipped 40 times (about 3 a year in the earlier years); its five longest sit-outs included two rallies of about 25% and one 28% fall; and random timing with the same exposure did as well or better 60% of the time.
entries.not_verified: One popular reading of one indicator (30 against 60 days, no price confirmation), mining power is an estimate and its day stamp is undocumented, and the sample holds only a few mining-stress episodes. Cash earned nothing in the test.

entries.name: Bitcoin only while US stocks are in an uptrend
entries.registered: commit edf2c7c; loader, runner and tests committed before the run (05ae19c)
entries.idea: Hold Bitcoin only on days when the Nasdaq Composite closed above its 200-day average (using the previous day's close); otherwise sit in cash.
entries.period: Last 30% of Bitcoin's history (2023-06-22 to 2026-11-13, never used to design the rule)

results.k: Random timing with the same exposure that did as well or better

conditions.rule: Sharpe at least 0.10 above holding
Beats 95% of randomly shifted copies of its own timing
Worst drop at least 10 points shallower than holding
Return above zero and at least 12 switches

entries.reading: In the earlier years (not judged) the filter sat out two big falls, late 2018 and 2022. In these years the Nasdaq stayed above its 200-day average 92% of the time, so the rule was nearly always in Bitcoin, sat out one 18% rally, and held through Bitcoin's worst fall because stocks kept rising; random timing with the same exposure did as well or better 73% of the time.
entries.not_verified: One popular rule (200 days, the Nasdaq, no confirmation); Bitcoin's link to stocks was weak before 2020; the earlier good years rest on two bear markets. Cash earned nothing in the test.
